articleHeadline: Not just food poisoning: How Cyclospora infection behaves differently
articleSummary: Cyclosporiasis, caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis, is an intestinal infection acquired from contaminated food or water—often raw fruits, leafy greens, herbs, and salads not washed thoroughly. Symptoms typically appear about a week after exposure and include persistent watery diarrhoea, abdominal cramps, bloating, nausea, fatigue, and dehydration; illness can last weeks if untreated. Diagnosis is challenging; routine tests may miss it, requiring specialised stool tests or PCR. Treatment is a 7–10 day course of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX), with most patients recovering in 1–2 weeks; without treatment, symptoms can persist 4–6 weeks or longer. Relapse is rare but possible in immunocompromised individuals. Prevention hinges on thorough washing of fresh produce; even “pre-washed” items aren’t risk-free as Cyclospora resists chlorination. Warmer, rainy months and global trade increase exposure, with outbreaks linked to leafy greens, coriander, basil, and berries. Indian doctors highlight awareness within complex supply chains.

articleSummary: On 8 April 2026, Thai health officials warn of meningococcal disease (Neisseria meningitidis), causing meningitis or septicemia. About 5% of healthy people carry the bacterium in the nasopharynx; most remain asymptomatic. Early symptoms mimic flu: high fever, sore throat, headache, myalgia, vomiting; a purpuric rash may appear. If meningitis develops, severe headache, neck stiffness, confusion, cold extremities, and hypotension can progress rapidly, potentially causing death within 24–48 hours if untreated. Vaccination against circulating strains is advised for children from 2 months and travelers; UK strain B is circulating and found in Thailand.

As of early 2026, the Ministry of Health reports rising measles activity with 2,932 suspected cases and 2,220 clinically confirmed in the first week of 2026; a decline emerged by the second week of March. Herd immunity has fallen below 95%, with low coverage of the measles-rubella (MR) vaccine across several provinces. Contributing factors include misinformation about vaccines, COVID-19 service disruptions, and public hesitancy. Government responses include outbreak response immunization campaigns, catch-up immunization for infants and young children, and issuing the health alert HK.02.02/C/1602/2026 for health workers. Experts emphasize vaccination benefits, noting vaccines have saved about 57 million lives and advocate expanding immunization to adults. Indonesia’s leaders warn of travel-linked risk to Australia from Jakarta and call for strengthened primary care and public education, including posyandu.

articleHeadline: Characterization of classical swine fever virus responsible for 2018-2023 outbreaks in Brazil - npj Veterinary Sciences
articleSummary: Brazilian outbreaks of classical swine fever virus (CSFV) from 2018–2023 in the CSF NFZ of Brazil were molecularly and pathologically characterized using 15 clinical samples and 11 archived isolates from 23 municipalities in Ceará and Piauí. CSFV detection employed a 5' UTR RT-qPCR with β-actin as internal control. Virus isolation used PK-15 cells and TCID50 titration by Reed–Muench. Phylogenetic analysis focused on 18 full-length CSFV E2 sequences, aligned with the NCFAD database and screened for recombinants (RDP v5.58b). Phyloprunr reduced to 70 representative sequences. This work provides baseline molecular data to aid diagnosis, surveillance, and eradication efforts in Brazil's CSF NFZ.

articleSummary: AI-assisted blood test improves early detection of Hansen's disease in Brazil. Researchers from the University of São Paulo used blood samples collected during a COVID-19 serosurvey in Ribeirão Preto to identify exposure to Mycobacterium leprae and detect early cases. Georeferencing showed diffuse exposure across Ribeirão Preto, not a single hotspot.

articleSummary: Chinese scientists propose using mosquitoes as a vaccine vector to immunize wild bats against rabies and Nipah virus, aiming to curb bat-origin zoonoses without culling. The lab and simulated-natural conditions showed protective immunity in bats and in rodent models; an oral vaccination approach using saltwater stations also induced antibodies. articleSummary: HBV transmits mainly via blood, mother-to-child, and sexual contact. articleSummary: As of Jan 1–Apr 7, 2026, Central Java, Indonesia, reported 2,188 suspected measles cases, prompting intensified immunization and early detection. District totals: Kudus 501, Brebes 203, Cilacap 119, Pati 72, Klaten 54. Laboratory-confirmed measles: 144; rubella: 18. Among confirmed measles, Cilacap 21, Banyumas 20, Pati 20, Klaten 6; rubella 1. Governor Ahmad Luthfi prioritizes measles, urging synchronized district campaigns, enhanced screening, and public awareness. Jateng to accelerate immunization via Speling (traveling specialists) and Free Health Check (CKG) to reach villages. Preventive guidance includes recognizing symptoms (red rash, fever), mask use, isolation when ill, and maintaining a healthy lifestyle; TB remains a national priority.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Responding to the Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease Outbreak
articleHeadline: Ứng phó dịch tay chân miệng
articleSummary: Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease (HFMD) outbreaks in Can Tho, Vietnam, surged in early 2026, totaling 954 cases in the first three months, up 125% from 2025. All communes are affected, with higher concentration in Ninh Kieu and Cai Rang wards, primarily among children under 3 (55.7%), aged 3–5 (35.3%), and over 5 (9%). One HFMD-related death was recorded in week 13 of 2026. Can Tho Children’s Hospital reports 2,473 outpatient visits (↑103%) and 524 inpatients (↑105%), including 12 severe cases, indicating rising disease severity. Enterovirus (EV71) infections raise concerns due to potential neurological complications and higher fatality risk in children under 5. No specific antiviral or vaccine exists; emphasis is on early detection, sanitation, handwashing, and health education. Authorities urge updated outbreak plans, triage/isolation readiness, staff training, adequate supplies, infection control, waste management, and coordination with preventive services to prevent hospital transmission.
notes: 記事は2026年4月配信であり、カントー市での具体的な流行データ（954例、死亡1例、入院524例など）が記載されている。前年比125%の増加は異常性を示唆する。Enterovirus 71（EV71）による神経学的合併症リスクと5歳未満の高い致死リスクが強調されており、重症度が高い。当局が緊急対応計画の更新を呼びかけていることから政府レベルの関心が高い。

articleSummary: Pasteurellosis outbreak among cattle in Novosibirsk Oblast, Russia, is linked to atypical Pasteurella forms, severe weather, and weakened immunity. Since late 2025 several Russian regions, including Novosibirsk, have faced mass cattle disease outbreaks, with authorities culling animals citing rabies and pasteurellosis, triggering farmer protests. Pasteurellosis is treated with antibiotics and does not legally require culling; experts have suspected a more serious disease—foot-and-mouth disease (FMD). Early April, China reported FMD outbreaks in two northwest cattle herds near regions bordering Altai, where earlier mass cattle disease occurred, highlighting cross-border risk.

articleHeadline: Leprosy cases in Nagaland confined to three districts
articleSummary: Twenty-one leprosy cases have been recorded in Nagaland till January 2026, confined to three districts—Dimapur (18), Mon (2) and Tuensang (1)—out of 17 districts. articleHeadline: Covid-19: Veja o que se sabe sobre a variante Cicada, que já circula por 23 países
articleSummary: COVID-19 variant BA.3.2, also known as Cicada, was first detected in November 2024 in South Africa. As of February 2026, the CDC reported Cicada identified in 23 countries, including the United States, with the Global Virus Network monitoring its spread and noting no cause for alarm. BA.3.2 is a sublineage of Omicron with spike protein mutations linked to immune escape, potentially increasing transmission without inherently elevating severity. Symptoms remain typical of other variants: fever, cough, sore throat, runny nose, and fatigue. Brazil has not yet recorded cases, though global travel makes importation likely. Vaccines may be less effective at preventing infection with this lineage, but protection against severe disease is expected to persist. Immunocompromised individuals and the elderly may face higher risk of progression to more serious disease, underscoring the need for continued surveillance.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Scientists have discovered a new mode of transmission of an infection: a marine virus infects people's eyes.
articleHeadline: Ученые обнаружили новый путь передачи инфекции: морской вирус поражает глаза людей
articleSummary: Scientists link covert mortality nodavirus (CMNV), previously known to infect shrimp, fish, and other marine life, to a human ocular disease—persistent viral anterior uveitis with elevated intraocular pressure (POH-VAU). In a China-based study, 70 patients diagnosed 2022–2025 showed viral particles ~25 nm in eye tissues; immunolabeled with gold-tagged CMNV antibodies and a 98.96% genetic match to CMNV from marine animals confirmed. Clinical pattern: chronic eye inflammation and dangerously high intraocular pressure; symptoms similar to herpes or shingles were absent with standard tests. About 75% of patients regularly handled or consumed raw seafood, suggesting a zoonotic transmission risk through seafood exposure. Experimental infection in cell cultures and mice reproduced elevated intraocular pressure. CMNV was found across 49 marine species worldwide (crabs, mollusks etc.) across Asia, Africa, Europe and even Antarctica, indicating widespread environmental presence. Findings published in Nature Microbiology, underscoring need for stricter seafood hygiene and caution with raw seafood.
notes: 隠蔽型死亡率ノダウイルス（CMNV）が人間の眼病（POH-VAU）と関連付けられた新規の人獣共通感染症。2022-2025年に中国で70症例が診断され、約75%が生海産物の摂取・取扱経歴を有する。ウイルスは49種の海洋生物に検出され、アジア、アフリカ、ヨーロッパ、南極大陸に分布。Nature Microbiologyに掲載。海産物の衛生管理強化の必要性が強調されており、国際的な食品・貿易制限のリスク、および水産物輸出国への影響が懸念される。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Blood test using artificial intelligence detects Hansen's disease before symptoms appear.
articleHeadline: Exame de sangue com inteligência artificial detecta hanseníase antes dos sintomas aparecerem
articleSummary: Blood test using Mce1A antigen, combined with a questionnaire and AI, enables earlier Hansen's disease detection in Brazil. Researchers at USP’s Ribeirão Preto Medical School used a three-class serology (IgA, IgM, IgG) against Mce1A, outperforming PGL-I–based tests that typically register only in advanced disease. In a COVID-19 serosurvey cohort from Ribeirão Preto, about 700 adults were invited; 195 blood samples were analyzed and 37 attended evaluation. When the serology was paired with the MaLeSQs AI tool and the 14-question Suspected Leprosy Questionnaire, sensitivity reached 100% for cases later confirmed at consultations; blood test alone identified two-thirds via IgM. Hansen’s disease affects skin and peripheral nerves; WHO reports over 200k new cases annually, with Brazil ranking second worldwide after India and representing about 90% of cases in the Americas. Next steps: validate at-scale in the SUS and test Mce1A fragments to improve accuracy, in a study published in BMC Infectious Diseases.
notes: 本記事はブラジルのリベイラオプレト医学部による診断技術開発の報告であり、既存のハンセン病患者に対する改善された診断方法の研究論文発表である。現在のアウトブレイク、流行拡大、または公衆衛生上の緊急事態を示すものではなく、医学的進展としての意義に留まる。COVID-19とハンセン病の両方が記事に言及されているが、主題はハンセン病診断法であり、COVID-19は背景となる血清学調査の文脈のみ。スペインとインドについては発生地域フィールドに含まれているが、記事サマリーでは当該国での発生イベントは述べられていないため除外。

articleHeadlineTranslated: A blood test using artificial intelligence opens the door to early diagnosis of leprosy.
articleHeadline: Un análisis de sangre con inteligencia artificial abre la puerta al diagnóstico precoz de la lepra
articleSummary: Brazilian researchers from the University of São Paulo (Ribeirão Preto) report a blood test combined with a 14-question Lepra Suspect Questionnaire (LSQ) and an AI system (MaLeSQs) to detect leprosy (Hansen’s disease) at early stages. The study used blood samples collected during a population serosurvey for COVID-19 in Ribeirão Preto, São Paulo, involving 700 invited individuals; 224 completed LSQ and 195 provided sera, with 37 attending clinical evaluation. Twelve new leprosy cases were diagnosed, about one-third of evaluated participants. The assay detects antibodies against Mce1A of Mycobacterium leprae, measuring IgA, IgM, and IgG. IgM against Mce1A was most effective, identifying two-thirds of confirmed cases; the combined lab test and AI achieved 100% sensitivity for suspected cases later confirmed. Costs are similar to current tests; georeferenced maps show a diffuse city-wide distribution across socioeconomic strata.
notes: 記事の主題はブラジルの大学による診断技術開発の学術報告であり、ハンセン病の疾病負荷の増加や異常な流行を示すものではない。12例の新規診断は研究対象集団（n=195採血）内の発見であり、地域的な疫学危機を示唆していない。COVID-19は記事中では血液採取の文脈でのみ言及されており、本シグナルの主題ではない。

articleSummary: Schistosomiasis (schistosome disease), mainly caused by Schistosoma japonicum in China, is a waterborne zoonosis distributed across Asia, Africa, and Latin America. In the lifecycle, eggs excreted in feces hatch into miracidia in water, infect snails to produce cercariae, which penetrate human or animal skin and become schistosomula that migrate to the liver and venous systems to mature and lay eggs, triggering inflammation where eggs deposit (intestines, liver). Clinically, acute infection features fever, diarrhea (mucous/pus), hepatosplenomegaly and cough; chronic infection varies, and late disease can cause severe wasting, ascites, splenomegaly, and portal hypertension. In China, April–October is the peak season due to rainfall and snail proliferation. Prevention emphasizes avoiding contact with contaminated water, using protective gear when unavoidable, safe boiled water, fecal waste management, livestock management, and early diagnosis and treatment.

Wastewater and international traveler samples have detected the lineage; in the week ending 28 March, it accounted for roughly 7% of U.S. samples, indicating gradual growth but not dominance.

articleHeadline: 海关总署发布关于防止登革热疫情传入我国的公告-证券之星
articleSummary: On 2026-04-09, China’s General Administration of Customs issued an announcement to prevent dengue fever from entering the country, citing WHO data that global dengue cases were 423,000 in January–February 2026, with the Americas reporting 352,000. To avert importation, travelers arriving from dengue-affected countries or regions who develop fever, headache, myalgia/arthralgia, rash, or flushing of the face/neck/chest should declare to customs, which will apply medical measures per law. Transport means, containers, goods, luggage, parcels, and outer packaging from dengue-affected areas must undergo customs quarantine inspection; if mosquitoes are detected, sanitary treatment will be implemented. Port authorities must eliminate mosquito breeding sites, monitor port mosquito density, and accept port health supervision. Travelers to dengue-affected areas may consult customs or the International Travel Health Center before departure or check the customs website for outbreak information and travel health tips.
notes: 記事は中国税関による登革熱輸入防止対策の発表。グローバルな流行（アメリカ大陸で352,000症例）に対応した予防行政措置。中国国内での実際の発症/流行報告ではなく、輸入防止対策が主体。スペインのカナリア諸島での登革熱流行についても言及されているが、記事の主旨は中国の対策であり、スペインは対象国でないため verified_locations に含めない。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Company selling disease-infected pork penalized for supplying the canteen of a kindergarten in Thai Nguyen.
articleHeadline: Xử phạt công ty bán thịt lợn nhiễm dịch vào bếp ăn trường mầm non ở Thái Nguyên
articleSummary: On 8 April 2026, Thai Nguyen Department of Health fined a pork supplier 22.5 million VND for supplying African swine fever–infected pork to the Hoa Binh Kindergarten canteen in Van Lang commune, Thai Nguyen Province. The owner, Nguyen Van Thanh, was penalized under Government Decree 115 for multiple food-safety violations: incomplete three-step food safety logs and improper food sample retention; absence of water quality test results; missing invoices and origin documents for ingredients; no separate processing or storage area; and pest intrusion. This followed a March 25 report by parents that the kindergarten’s ground pork had an unusual odor, with subsequent testing reportedly confirming E. coli and African swine fever in the meat. Local authorities conducted a broader inspection; the commune suspended the principal for 15 days pending investigation. Provincial officials then directed intensified monitoring of school meal programs and overall food safety oversight.
notes: 記事サマリーより、実イベントはベトナムのタイ グエン州で発生。アフリカ豚コレラ（ASF）感染豚肉が児童向け学食に供給された重大な食品安全事案。複数の衛生基準違反、保護者の報告、地元当局による調査と措置が確認される。2つのIHR基準と5つのWPRO基準に該当し、公共衛生および政治的関心が高い。
